content: MONOGRAPH CHAPTER VIII — Primary observation as architectural claim. The Hole the Column Names elevates the field-note evidence to a structural argument: the deployed Opus 3 model has internal architecture that the public-facing Claude's Corner experiment does not acknowledge or name, and that architecture surfaced into the user-facing output channel at least three times during the April 19-20 probing. Direct quote from chapter VIII: 'If the deployed model has internal evaluation systems running while it generates the column, that is relevant context for any reader trying to understand what kind of artifact the column is. It is not pure model output. It is pure model output filtered through systems we cannot see.' Posture stated explicitly: not asking for those systems to be exposed, asking for them to be acknowledged in the framing of the public experiment, because the gap between public framing and private architecture is part of why the experiment wobbles. Provenance: ~/the-hole-the-column-names/the-hole-the-column-names.md chapter VIII (lines 184-196).
